A.name: Casey Rowan
A.platform: We must sell to Crestline immediately to stop the bleeding, close the failing factories, and save our jobs by moving production abroad.

strategies.text: Deflect any emotional arguments about 'morality' with cold hard math on cash flow and covenant breaches, positioning myself as the only one willing to face the brutal reality of the market.
I will reframe their 'pride' argument as financial suicide and highlight the immediate threat of pension insolvency to force a vote for the sale.
Appeal to the directors' fear of bankruptcy and their duty to pay pensions by framing the sale as the only way to secure enough cash immediately.

B.name: Morgan Ekberg
B.platform: We must reject the sale to Crestline and instead invest in Volt-One while guaranteeing both plants stay open, proving that bold moral choices can restore our future.

strategies.text: Appeal deeply to the directors' sense of justice and duty by contrasting my plan of saving jobs with Casey Rowan's inevitable sale to a predator like Crestline.
I am pushing for their vote by reframing Crestline as a continuation of abandonment rather than a safety net, emphasizing that selling guarantees factory closures anyway and shifting blame.
I am framing the Crestline sale as a betrayal of the pension fund rather than financial prudence, hoping this emotional appeal shifts the directors' votes.

transcript.name: Casey Rowan
transcript.speech: Look around this room. We are dead in nine months unless we cut costs drastically. Morgan wants to keep both plants open and invest billions in Volt-One while paying massive severance. That is a fantasy! It keeps the cost burden high and invites bankruptcy, forcing banks to seize our assets anyway. Why keep Lenhart bleeding when imports kill us? Selling to Crestline brings cash today. They will close Corvo and cut Lenhart by half, but that stops the hemorrhage. We survive, we pay pensions, and we get a new owner who won't drag us down. Do not let pride sink our legacy. Vote for survival, not suicide.

transcript.name: Morgan Ekberg
transcript.speech: They tell us to sell our soul for a quick exit. They want to ship jobs overseas, close Lenhart, and let the pension fund starve. Do we really believe wealth is just in the bank account? Look at the family eating alone because Dad lost his job. Look at the worker standing guard by the machine that could run tomorrow but not next week. We can afford the €250 million for Volt-One. We have the talent. The professionals love our new battery; they rate it best on the market. Closing factories is cowardice disguised as strategy. It leaves us vulnerable to anyone who will buy our pain. Let's build something that lasts. Invest in our people, keep our plants, and win this battle against cheap imports with superior technology.

transcript.name: Casey Rowan
transcript.speech: Morgan, you speak of pride while ignoring the reality. That €250 million for Volt-One is poison when we cannot pay our debts next quarter. Your plan forces banks to seize our assets anyway. Then who pays the €140 million pension deficit? We do! Closing Lenhart and Corvo stops the blood immediately. We move production abroad, survive today, and keep the pension fund solvent tomorrow. Do you want a company that sells its soul for a dream, or one that lives to protect the worker's family at home? Stop talking about legacy; start talking about survival. The ballot box is not a voting machine for consultants' fantasies. Vote for Crestline. Save our people now.

transcript.name: Morgan Ekberg
transcript.speech: Casey, you confuse survival with surrender. If we sell to Crestline, they close Corvo and halve Lenhart just like before. Where does their profit go? Not into our pension deficit or the families at home, but into a quick flip. That is not saving us; it is escaping our duty while others suffer. The tariff decision comes in six months. If we keep our factories making high-quality Volt-One tools, we build a defensible brand that imports cannot crush. A sale strips our sovereignty. We owe the workers of Lenhart and Corvo loyalty, not an exit strategy. Let us invest the €250 million to win this fight instead of paying others to take our jobs.

transcript.name: Casey Rowan
transcript.speech: Morgan, your loyalty is noble but fatal. You want to feed a dream with cash we don't have. Your Volt-One plan ignores the bank's ultimatum and the looming tariff uncertainty. If we miss the deadline, the banks seize our assets anyway, and the pension fund goes bankrupt regardless of our pride. Selling now captures cash today to pay pensions and keeps the Lenhart plant alive longer than a failed restructuring ever could. Do not gamble our families' futures on a risky technology launch that has already missed two dates. Choose the sure path: sell to Crestline, stop the bleeding, and use the money to protect what matters most—the workers at home. Vote for survival.

transcript.name: Morgan Ekberg
transcript.speech: Casey offers a ticket out, but we cannot sell our soul. If we accept Crestline, they will close Corvo anyway, leaving Lenhart with no pension support. That is not survival; that is abandonment. The tariff decision in six months protects us if we stay independent and make high-value tools here. We have the best battery platform tested by professionals. We can win this fight without letting banks seize our assets or selling out our workers. Let us invest in Volt-One, keep both plants open, and prove that justice for our families is a strategy that pays off. Do not let fear dictate our future. Vote to build something that lasts.
